title: Locally Noetherian schemes
statement:
A scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] is *locally Noetherian* if it admits an affine open
covering $X=\bigcup_iU_i$ with $\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] for all
$i$ (*Stacks Project, Properties, Definition 28.5.1, Tag
[01OV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01OV)*). Remark: open subschemes of locally Noetherian schemes are locally
Noetherian, since an immersion is locally of finite type (Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.15.5, Tag
[01T5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01T5)) and a scheme locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian scheme is locally Noetherian (Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.15.6, Tag
[01T6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01T6)). A locally Noetherian morphism situation is one where the
target is locally Noetherian.

split_report.summary: Checked the definition against Stacks Morphisms Lemma 29.15.6, Tag 01T6, and Lemma 29.15.5, Tag 01T5. The statement is retained: it defines locally Noetherian schemes by an affine cover with Noetherian coordinate rings, records that open subschemes remain locally Noetherian, and names the convention that a locally Noetherian morphism situation has locally Noetherian target. Mathlib provides IsLocallyNoetherian, the affine-open-cover equivalence, and the open-immersion preservation theorem, but the equivalence between the Stacks definition and the Mathlib class is theorem-level, so this remains a split definition with a mathlib_candidate and no new nodes. The only statement dependency is the scheme notion.
split_report.blueprint: The item is the blueprint node pqf-def-locnoeth itself; its full definition and the two Stacks consequences are realized here.

The agreement of the Stacks definition with Mathlib's class is therefore theorem-level rather than a one-line definitional match.
